scale_cues: The white dinner plate is roughly 26 to 28 cm across and was used as the main scale reference. Food portions were estimated against the plate's surface area and the thickness of the steak slices. A fork is partly visible at the top-left edge but was not used for measurement.
assumptions: Plate diameter is about 27 cm for scale.
Steak is beef and cooked to medium-rare to medium.
The centerpiece is a breaded or herb-crusted lean protein; chicken breast was chosen as the closest FDC match, but white fish is possible.
The pale mash is potato-based with butter and milk; a cauliflower-potato blend is possible.
Weights are edible cooked masses, excluding plate and bones.
Dressing and cooking fat are inferred from the visual sheen and preparation, not directly measured.
Red onion slivers and small bits are under 5 g and were not listed separately.
